England captain Harry Kane, speaking to ITV: “An incredible gesture, reception at the start of the game. Once the game starts, it’s about getting the win, getting the three points. We’re playing against a tough team, a team that wanted to prove something tonight.

“I think for large spells of the game we done well. Got a little bit tired towards the end but overall a really great win and sets up a great game on Sunday now.”

On how he was feeling as he stepped up for his penalty: “Same as ever. I missed my last one for Bayern, so I think it’s always important to try and bounce back with the next one. Try to not miss two in a row but executing. I practised yesterday like I always do and it’s just about going out there and doing it out on the pitch.

“I think we gave away a few too many easy balls, especially in our own half, which killed the momentum a little bit. I think we had enough chances to score two or three but we’re playing against a good team.

“We’re in the midst of a run of tough games for club and country, so you can’t always expect things to be perfect. Of course, we know we can improve on a few bits and we will need to if we want to win on Sunday, but ultimately it’s about getting a win tonight.”

On aiming to beat Spain and top the group: “100%. After the first game when we lost here against them, we knew we left a bit out there. We knew we could’ve done a bit better. We said to ourselves let’s win every game until the next one and see what happens. It’s the perfect opportunity now on Sunday to try and prove ourselves.”

Thomas Tuchel tells ITV: “A good win, we wanted this desperately, we deserved it. It was hard work against a good opponent.” We will bring you more from the England head coach shortly.

Harry Kane has told ITV that it was an “incredible reception” for him at the start of a “really good win”. We will bring you the captain’s full quotes shortly.

While top spot in the group is still up for grabs, England have booked their place in the Nations League quarter-finals, which will take place in March 2027.

The winners of those ties progress to the Nations League Finals in June.

Harry Kane has now scored 92 goals in 126 appearances for England.

Thomas Tuchel has said he has “unfinished business” with England and will remain in his position for the Euros in 2028, but did say that he would return to club football after seeing out his contract.

“I signed the contract, I want to stay until the Euros,” he said this week. “I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business.”

But he added: “I miss the 50 matches [a season].

“I miss the two minutes when everything is done. You go out two minutes before the whistle goes, it’s like the best two minutes, everything is done and you’re in a full stadium, lights are on and you’re just so excited and you’re part of it.”

Shortly before kick-off, Croatia captain Luka Modric will present England captain Harry Kane with a special gift from the Croatian Football Federation (HNS), marking his Ballon d’Or win and his achievement in becoming England’s all-time record appearance holder with 126 caps.

Modric is not in the starting line-up but the 41-year-old has 206 caps for his country and will present Kane with a specially crafted replica of the first football ever brought to Croatia, which English industrialists introduced to the town of Zupanja in 1880. This event is regarded as the beginning of organised football on Croatian soil.

England’s 3-0 home victory over Czech Republic last month left them on nine points after four Nations League group games.

It came after a 2-0 win in the away contest, a 7-0 thumping of Croatia and a 3-2 defeat against world champions Spain.

A draw tonight will be enough for Thomas Tuchel’s side to book their place in the quarter-finals of the competition.

The eight teams to finish in the top two of the four League A groups will play in the knockout rounds that start in March 2027.

The two worst sides to finish bottom are automatically relegated, while the other bottom sides and third-placed sides are at risk of relegation via a play-off.

Few expect Jobe to be better than his older brother. While Jobe will make his England debut just two months after turning 21, Jude’s first cap came aged 17. By the time that he was Jobe’s age now, Jude had already thrived for England in two international tournaments. But Jobe has one major sporting advantage: he is the younger sibling.

Younger siblings have significantly more chance of becoming elite athletes. If two siblings both become professional, the little sibling is significantly more likely to enjoy the better career.

Jude and Jobe Bellingham could become the first brothers to start for England since Gary and Phil Neville took to the field together 19 years ago, with Jobe included in his first senior squad.

Jack and Bobby Charlton are the only other brothers to play together for England in the post-war period.

“I can’t ignore it, but obviously with Jude being here too, it’s a great, great feeling for the family,” Jobe said on the FA’s England app as he discussed his call-up.

“It’s quite special, to be honest. It’s such a huge bonus on top of something that’s already so special and so great. To be called up for England is a dream itself and I’ve been so proud to have the opportunity to represent England at every age group.

“I always enjoyed coming away with England, I love competing against top players at whichever age group. But to have that chance of an opportunity to represent England with my brother, it’s really hard to put into words.

“I don’t have the words, really. I think it’s only emotion that could describe it, and, hopefully, if that time does come, you’ll see a lot of emotion from people, and definitely from my family.”

There will be a special pre-match presentation to honour Harry Kane becoming England’s record appearance maker, with 126 caps, overtaking Peter Shilton. Shilton has held the record since 1989.

The goalkeeper is at Wembley to formally mark Kane’s achievement. The England captain will also show the Ballon d’Or trophy he won last month.

Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph from last month will also be celebrated tonight before kick-off, along with his record appearance.

“I think I maybe underappreciated how big it was going to be, how big the reaction was going to be,” he told the BBC.

“It’s just been crazy, whether it’s messages on my phone or on social media, or people calling me, and just being in the street and everyone congratulating me.

“I think the actual moment when Ronaldo said my name, it’s strange, it’s almost like a movie.

“In the moment, it was like in slow motion and the confetti was supposed to fall and all this, but when I watched it back, I had my hand to my mouth and maybe a couple of seconds and I was out, but in the actual moment, it felt like I was doing it for a minute.

“It was a really unique feeling because it is different to playing a game or scoring a goal, because it is so individual, it is nothing you can kind of do.

“Your mind is playing games with you the whole night, whether it is going to be you or not.

“So, when he actually said my name, it was just a crazy emotion.”

To the exclusive club of Billy Wright, Sir Bobby Charlton, Bobby Moore and Peter Shilton, the name Harry Kane will be added on Thursday night. It is only the fifth time that a new men’s England international appearance record has been set in the post-war era, with Kane preparing for his 126th England match to surpass a landmark that has stood for 36 years.

“I’ll be the first to congratulate him because I think he’s done it the right way,” says Shilton, who will be back at Wembley to metaphorically pass on the baton.

“He’s not coming on as a substitute; he’s been out there every game, doing his job. Records are there to be beaten and I couldn’t think of anybody better than Harry, not just on the pitch but off the pitch. I am very proud of the record and handing it to Harry makes it not quite as bad.

“I think striker is the hardest position to play and goalkeeper is the second hardest because of the responsibility you’ve got. But scoring goals is the most difficult thing and Harry’s record in the modern game is there to be seen.”

Thomas Tuchel has said Harry Kane was the deserved winner of the Ballon d’Or, with the England head coach describing the striker as “an extraordinary player”.

“He wins the Ballon d’Or, and deservedly so, and in the next game for England he gets the all-time record with 126 matches,” Tuchel said when announcing the latest squad.

“Thursday is a deserved occasion to celebrate an extraordinary player.”

Kane said: “It’s not about me – it’s about the team. I love coming to every England camp. I love playing every game and representing the country in the best way possible.”

Harry Kane starts for England in what will be a record 126th appearance for his country.

Thomas Tuchel makes three changes from last month’s win over Czech Republic, with Dan Burn, Declan Rice and Anthony Gordon replacing Marc Guehi, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Eberechi Eze.

Harry Kane will become England’s record appearance maker this evening, with the 33-year-old set to earn his 126th cap.

The striker started his international career against Lithuania in March 2015, scoring just 79 second after replacing Wayne Rooney at Wembley.

Eight years later, Kane surpassed Rooney as the country’s record goalscorer, netting his 54th England goal in an away contest with Italy.

He equalled Peter Shilton’s record of 125 caps last month against Czech Republic as he scored his 90th and 91st international goals.

England will be hoping for a repeat of their fixture against Croatia last month, with Thomas Tuchel’s side producing an emphatic 7-0 victory in Rijeka.

England were 4-0 up at half-time of the Nations League contest, which was attended by 6,000 schoolchildren and 100 visiting fans, with Croatia supporters sanctioned over previous bad behaviour.

England’s front four of Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka were all on the scoresheet in the opening period, with Kane and Saka doubling their tallies in the second half before a late seventh from Morgan Rogers.

Good evening and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of England vs Croatia in the Nations League, with the hosts’ captain Harry Kane set to become the country’s most-capped player.

The 33-year-old has enjoyed a memorable few weeks, becoming the first English Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years and following it up with a new Bayern Munich contract, and an appearance at Wembley tonight will take him clear of Peter Shilton’s record of 125 England caps.

Kane scored twice in his record-equalling appearance against Czech Republic at Wembley last month, extending his international tally to 91 goals – a total that is unrivalled for England.

“It’s not about me – it’s about the team,” Kane said before tonight’s landmark moment. “I love coming to every England camp. I love playing every game and representing the country in the best way possible.”

The 3-0 home victory over Czech Republic left England on nine points after four Nations League group games, with a 2-0 win in the away contest and a 7-0 thumping of Croatia coming after a 3-2 defeat against world champions Spain.

Thomas Tuchel will be hoping that his side can inflict another heavy defeat on Croatia this evening, but a draw will be enough to book their place in the quarter-finals, with the group’s top two teams progressing.

While Kane will collect plaudits for his 126th cap, attention will also be on a potential first, with Jude Bellingham’s younger brother, Jobe, included in a senior England squad for the first time.

The two Bellinghams appearing together in a senior match would be a new experience for them, while it would be the first time that brothers have taken to the field together for England in 19 years.

“I can’t ignore it, but obviously with Jude being here too, it’s a great, great feeling for the family,” Jobe said on the Football Association’s England app. “It’s quite special, to be honest. It’s such a huge bonus on top of something that’s already so special and so great.”

#937. Continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

We’re sharing this article early to provide faster access to peer-reviewed, accepted research. It is citable and carries a permanent DOI. This version is subject to further edits and will be replaced automatically by the final Version of Record. All legal disclaimers apply.

Current state-of-the-art peptide synthesis faces a significant global challenge in efficiency and sustainability.1 With demand for peptide therapeutics growing rapidly,2,3 our ability to provide these important medicines is under increasing pressure.4 Chemical synthesis typically proceeds C-to-N and requires protecting groups, whereas ribosomal synthesis proceeds N-to-C from unprotected amino acids (AAs). To improve efficiency and sustainability, we developed a continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis (NCPS) using N-/C-unprotected AAs or fragments without intermediate isolations, achieving ≥95% average yield per coupling and ≤1.0% epimerization. The method enabled seven consecutive couplings. Starting from N-/C-unprotected AAs, peptide assembly requires fewer isolations than those needed to prepare the corresponding Fmoc-AA building blocks before conventional synthesis can begin. This method accepts all 20 canonical AAs and a wide range of non-canonical AAs important for drug-like profiles.5 Longer peptides can be readily assembled through continuous fragment coupling while maintaining chiral integrity. This approach reduces isolations by ~10-fold and waste generation by up to ~100-fold. We further developed a flow synthesizer that enhances speed and productivity while mitigating batch manufacturing risks. The method enabled the synthesis of a tirzepatide heptapeptide fragment, degarelix, a 14-mer engineered macrocyclic peptide, and semaglutide. Overall, continuous NCPS has the potential to transform peptide manufacturing.

#934. What's going on with the polar vortex?

Observations show the ring of fierce winds that rotate at the Earth's North Pole has changed direction. Scientists say it's a historic disruption and the earliest reversal on record. What could it mean for the weather?

High up in the atmosphere, there's a ring of cold air swirling over the Arctic that can intensify, weaken, and shapeshift through the seasons. This is the polar vortex.

If it gets disrupted, this twisting pool of chilly air can influence the weather we experience, increasing the risk of a cold snap in the Northern Hemisphere.

Current observations show the vortex has weakened unprecedentedly early this year, with its winds reversing directions.

It's not yet clear how the current disruption to the polar vortex will affect the Northern Hemisphere winter, but scientists agree it is a record-breaking event.

"As far as we know, this is the earliest stratospheric vortex disruption that has been observed," European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecast (ECMWF) principal scientists Tim Stockdale and Frederic Vitart told the AFP news agency.

The French meteorological agency Meteo-France, meanwhile, called it "an unprecedented event."

The early breakdown of the vortex "really increases the chance of cold air outbreaks across the latitudes where most of the densely populated population centers are across the Northern Hemisphere, US, Europe and East Asia," Judah Cohen, a climatologist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology told AFP.

The polar vortex is an enormous band of cold, low-pressure air that spins counterclockwise around the North Pole, about 10 to 50 kilometers (around 6 to 30 miles) above the surface.

It's closely connected to the jet stream, another band of powerful winds just below the vortex. The jet stream forms a boundary where the cold Arctic air meets warmer air from the tropics and subtropics.

The vortex can sometimes be a tight circle, keeping the coldest air locked around the North Pole over winter. It can also form uneven waves that dip southwards. And as it changes in strength and shape, that can influence the atmosphere below and alter the position of the jet stream, which drives the weather on the ground.

So, if the jet stream is more "wavy," and plunges south, it may also allow freezing Arctic air to spill southward.

One of the biggest influences that can provoke this kind of disruption is known as "sudden stratospheric warming." This is when temperatures in the polar stratosphere rise dramatically within a few days, causing the vortex's strong westerly winds to weaken.

This can push the vortex off its spot at the North Pole, make it split apart into multiple rings, or — as is happening now — cause the westerly winds to change direction.

It can take several weeks for the vortex to recover.

A previous polar vortex disruption contributed to the deadly Great Texas Freeze in February 2021, which caused more than a week of freezing temperatures that sparked power outages and killed hundreds of people.

But bone-chilling cold isn't a foregone conclusion. The Met Office, which is the UK's national weather and climate service, stresses that what's happening with the polar vortex can nudge odds in that direction, but it's not a switch that turns cold weather on and off.

Other weather patterns can also influence the outcome.

For example, there's a possibility El Nino, which is associated with milder winters, could "moderate or modify" the impacts, Cohen told AFP. But he added this was not certain.

The El Nino weather phenomenon, caused by the warming of surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is currently intensifying and is expected to peak at the end of the year. The ongoing event has been classified as exceptionally strong and is disrupting weather around the globe.

Some research has also linked the rapid warming of the Arctic driven by climate change to increasing disruptions to the polar vortex. That means that, even as the planet warms, some areas may still experience more severe cold spells. But this connection is not conclusive and is still debated by scientists.

#932. The dangers of revising Europe's security architecture

Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

European leaders have so far found compromises in response to many of US President Donald Trump's demands.

But they were surprised to hear Trump say that he raised Europe's security framework with Russian officials.

"It's going to be a big agreement and it's going to involve more than Ukraine," Trump said after meeting Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House last week.

He said that deal might include all of Europe. But what he meant by "all of Europe" was not clear.

US envoy Jared Kushner also wrote that Europe and Russia had struggled to establish a sustainable security framework for more than 30 years and that he was looking at "broader" European security architecture before he was to fly to Abu Dhabi.

That sent off alarm bells in European capitals, with diplomats having pushed back on Washington's approach to secure a peace deal in Ukraine.

They feared that a peace settlement could restore Russia's sphere of influence and undermine NATO.

"We ​already have European security ​architecture in place. NATO and the European Union both have their ​respective roles. We ​must make sure Ukraine is integrated ‌into ⁠this architecture," said Kaja Kallas, the European Union's foreign policy chief.

Russia made clear during talks in Abu Dhabi earlier this week that they were keen to discuss a broader European security framework before tackling the specifics of the war.

"Phrases about the European security architecture are certainly Russian talking points and not only talking points but, to a degree, part of a media propaganda effort that Russia makes to frame the war as it wishes to frame the war," said Michael Kimmage, a historian of the Cold War.

Russian leaders, including Vladimir Putin, have long alleged that the US and NATO repeatedly violated pledges they made in the early 1990s not to expand the alliance into the former Soviet bloc.

They have seen NATO's enlargement during this period as having put them in a humiliating position in which they could do very little.

At the same time, in the 1990s, the European project saw the birth of the European Union, the single market that ensured the free movement of goods and people across member states, the Schengen agreement for border-free travel, and the euro.

The core idea was to extend peace across the continent.

"Europe can mean so many things, but the European project was not designed for war. It was designed for peace," said Kimmage.

During this period, there were even suggestions of Russia becoming a NATO member.

But that relative period of stability changed after Russia invaded Georgia in 2008, annexed Crimea in 2014 and launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

"Russia wants to redraw all of this by force. And I think that that's fundamentally unacceptable to Europe with all the diversity and variations that you get within the European landscape on what's acceptable and not acceptable. I think the large-scale redrawing of borders by force is just not the European project," said Kimmage.

"So to the extent that the redrawing of borders by force is the lifeblood of Russian foreign policy, and I think that's a pretty easy case to make, Russia and Europe are at an impasse," he said.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The Trump administration very quickly turned to making sure that "existing European security institutions" would be intact, with Jared Kushner having said late Thursday that the next round of negotiations would include "our European partners."

Kushner, along with Steve Witkoff, flew to Moscow to talk to Putin after talks in Abu Dhabi. Then they flew to Dublin, Ireland, to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Kushner had earlier Thursday signaled some "really incredible" postwar plans for Ukraine, saying that it could not be concluded without Europeans at the table.

"We should not allow a diktat from Russia that would result in some kind of neutralization or significant reduction in the military forces of Ukraine going forward, because that would make Ukraine very, very vulnerable to future aggression and pressure coming from Russia," said Hiski Haukkala, the director of the Finnish Institute of International Affairs.

That would mean that Ukraine would also be completely dependent on the security guarantees that the US or Europeans are able and willing to provide.

"We are supporting Ukraine because we are supporting international law and the basic norms of decency and international security when it comes to European security architecture. And this is the vantage point from which we are operating," he said.

The European Union has repeatedly pointed to some of the basic treaties that Russia broke, including:

"Russia walked away from these principles and smashed them to pieces in the process. And they are not interested in reinstating the previous security architecture order. They want something different in its stead. And as long as this is not on the table, the Russian form of negotiation is to wage war. War is a form of bargaining," Haukkala said.

"And they are signaling strategic intent to change the makeup of European security, to subdue Ukraine and to change the very essence of European security," he added.

Daniel Fried, a former assistant secretary of state for European Affairs in the George W. Bush administration, said Russia is very good at sticking to its demands.

He said Russians know how to negotiate and "right now, they are not negotiating," referring to talks in Abu Dhabi.

Some experts said there was no possibility of having a new security architecture with the Russians at this point because there was no trust or common vision to align with Russia at the moment.

"There is no obvious compromise — dismantling NATO and the EU is not an option for Europe," said Maria Snegovaya, an expert on Russia at the Center for Strategic and International Studies think tank.

"Repeatedly offering Putin peace deals he is unwilling to accept will not produce that outcome," Snegovaya said.

Others like Balazs Jarabik, an expert on post-Soviet politics, said that Russia was part of the European security architecture whether Europeans liked it or not.

"And the question is whether it's included as our enemy. Obviously, Russia is not going to be a partner, right? We have to find a modus operandi to reduce the risk of a horizontal escalation and potentially a bigger European war, even a bigger one than what we have now."

A host of European leaders on Friday rejected the Russian demands to discuss Europe's security framework as well, with a spokesperson for the German government saying that Berlin was looking to host a meeting of the "Coalition of the Willing" to secure funding for Ukraine's defense and reach a unified position regarding future peace talks.

Thomas Tuchel may not have planned it this way, but in one night he gave us all the rich history of the England team at once: some glorious attacking football, some self-sabotage defending, a red card, a late siege and a fight.

This was the beguiling story of Spain 2 England 3, an evening that began with the world champions parading the World Cup trophy and ended with 10 Englishmen defending a lead with their last breath. England beat the world champions in Madrid, and for more than 30 minutes including injury time they did so with 10 men, Dan Burn heading the last ball out as per the tradition of a defensive rearguard action.

This was the game that had it all: including a substitute, in Djed Spence, who had already picked up a yellow card on the bench before he came on. It was a coming-of-age performance in goal for James Trafford. So too for Ben White, the 2022 World Cup departee who scored the third and lunged with astonishing effect in the 84th minute to block a Nico Williams shot.

Thomas Tuchel will speak openly to England’s players about what they should do if they encounter racism in the Nations League Group 3 decider with Spain.

This is the first time England have faced Spain in Madrid since November 2004 when they were beaten 1-0 in the Santiago Bernabéu, a game that was ravaged by obscene chanting. The nations were supposed to play a fixture in the Spanish capital in 2008, but the Football Association insisted it be moved to Seville instead.

Earlier this year, Spanish supporters brought shame on themselves again after a flurry of anti-Muslim chants marred a friendly against Egypt; they were fined $20,000 by Fifa and must play their next friendly in a partially closed stadium.

There will be a full house in the Wanda Metropolitano on Sunday night, as the reigning world and European champions aim to defend their extraordinary unbeaten run of 43 games, and England head coach Tuchel is adamant the atmosphere will be in keeping with the occasion.

The German has, however, made it clear he and his staff will use their platform before the contest to remind England’s players of the steps they should take if the worst scenario unfolds.

Asked about incidents that had pockmarked this fixture before, Tuchel said: “I think I hear it the first time that this happens. I think it’s unacceptable. In any stadium, not even in stadiums, we will never accept racism. We will never be racist towards anyone.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of England’s final Nations League Group 3 decider as Thomas Tuchel’s side take on Spain at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid.

Although both countries are safely through to the quarter-finals, England will seek revenge on Spain, who beat them in the Euro 2024 final and in their previous Nations League face-off on September 26 at Wembley. That day, Luis de la Fuente’s men profited from Harry Kane’s uncharacteristic penalty miss, England’s general wastefulness in front of goal and some seriously lacklustre defending to earn a chaotic 3-2 comeback victory after falling 2-1 behind at half-time.

Since that defeat, England have won four successive Nations League fixtures against the Czech Republic and Croatia by an aggregate score of 14-1. Last time out, they beat Croatia on Thursday, earning a 2-1 win as Kane, who became England’s most-capped men’s player with 126 appearances, dispatched a second-half penalty to seal the three points. Spearheaded by the Ballon d’Or holder’s brilliance, England must win this evening in order to overtake Spain and top the group.

Speaking ahead of the match, Tuchel said: “I think we are ready to win. And then you can never predict the result in football, never. But it’s important that we show the mindset that you speak of and the spirit, and we will. I’m very confident about that.”

#930. Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?

Should young people in Germany be more worried about their future than Baby Boomers were in the 1980s and 1990s? Or should both generations take to the streets and protest together? DW checked the data.

Young people across Germany and Europe are taking to the streets, voicing fears of a bleak future.

But is that really the case? Does Gen Z face greater challenges than Baby Boomers did in the 1990s? What do the two generations have in common, and where do their experiences differ?

"Of course, it's fair to ask, 'Were things just as tough for you back then?'" youth researcher Simon Schnetzer tells DW. "But young people see that things are difficult for them now, and say that's why they need support today."

Schnetzer, who wrote the annual Youth in Germany study, highlights one key question raised by the recent demonstrations across Europe as: "Have we given young people the conditions they need to live and work here with confidence, and to keep this system funded?"

His straightforward answer is no. A survey of the statistics shows that both Gen Z and the Baby Boomers are affected by major societal changes, but in different ways. DW surveyed data on pensions, education, housing and climate change to find out more.

The facts point to a clear trend: Fewer and fewer young people are having to support an ever-growing number of retirees. According to the Germany's public pension insurance system, there were 3.73 contributors for every retiree in 1957. By 2025, that figure had fallen to just 2.1.

By 2045, this number is projected to drop to just 1.73 contributors per retiree. In absolute terms, this means 35.35 million contributors will be financing pensions for 16.82 million retirees.

To cushion this trend and keep contribution rates stable, the pension system already receives around €118 billion [$131 billion] in annual government subsidies. This amounts to roughly 25% of the federal budget. That means an increasing share of the population will be called upon to help fund pensions.

There are also signs that many people's pensions are already falling short of covering their living expenses. The number of retirees relying on federal basic income support has risen from 257,000 in 2003 to 738,000 in 2024.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Rising rents hit low-income households particularly hard. According to a report by the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW), the share of income spent on rent by low-income households rose from around 24% in 1990 to nearly 36% in 2021.

This means that in 2021, the lowest-income households spent an average of 14 percentage points more of their income on rent than high-income households.

According to Germany's Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), in 2025, an average of 11% of the population spent more than 40% of their disposable income on housing costs. Among people at risk of poverty, the figure was as high as 35%.

However, according to calculations by real estate platform Jacasa, Boomers could actually help ease pressure on the housing market in the coming years. They currently own around 4.8 million owner-occupied houses and apartments.

Over the coming decades, these properties are expected to change hands as former occupants sell them, move into assisted living, or hand them down through inheritance. In some regions, this could lead to an oversupply of properties and, consequently, lower prices, according to Jacasa's projections.

According to the federal government's Education Finance Report, public spending on education for people under 30 has doubled since 2011, rising from around €4,000 to approximately €8,000 per person annually.

Despite this increase, Germany ranks only in the middle of the pack internationally. According to the Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), public education spending accounted for 4.6% of Germany's gross domestic product (GDP) in 2022, compared with an OECD average of 4.7%.

However, the additional funding cannot solve the problem of teacher shortages. According to estimates by the Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education and Cultural Affairs, Germany will be short of around 27,000 teachers by 2035. The main reasons are the wave of Baby Boomer retirements and declining birth rates, which have contributed to a shortage of young teachers.

Back in 1972, the Club of Rome warned of the consequences of global warming in its landmark publication The Limits to Growth. According to the United Nations, the planet is on track for 2.6°C of warming by the end of the century compared with pre-industrial levels.

If the world maintains its current climate policies, children who are six years old today could experience heat waves two to seven times as often as Boomers did over their lifetimes. That was the finding of a 2025 study by Vrije University in Brussels.

The deadly impact of extreme weather is already evident in rising death tolls during recent heatwaves. According to Germany's Robert Koch Institute (RKI), an estimated 16,000 people died from heat-related causes across Germany by mid-September 2026. The vast majority — more than 14,000 — were over the age of 65.

"Gen Z and Baby Boomers are in the same boat. We need to bring them together, because otherwise younger people have no prospects for prosperity, and neither do older generations," youth researcher Schnetzer concludes.

He suggests that both generations take to the streets and protest together, adding that would just be the beginning. "What needs to follow is a constructive process to define goals and measures that everyone can support," he said. "Even if it means making sacrifices."

This article was originally published in German.

#929. Mikel Arteta confirms David Raya doesn’t need surgery in huge Arsenal injury boost

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Raya hurt his shoulder in a seemingly innocuous collision with William Osula in Arsenal’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Mikel Arteta has provided an injury update on David Raya after Arsenal’s first-choice goalkeeper was forced off with a shoulder problem against Newcastle.

Raya was hurt in a seemingly innocuous collision with Magpies striker William Osula from a corner, departing the field clutching his left arm in visible agony. He was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga in the 70th minute of the 2-2 draw at St James’ Park.

Arteta confirmed after the match that the 31-year-old would have an MRI scan on Sunday and said his withdrawal was “never good news”.

Amid fears that Raya had suffered a serious injury, there were rumblings that the goalkeeper had escaped with a knock on the nerve, which would rule him out for a significantly shorter period.

He was nevertheless missing from an open training session on Monday as Arsenal prepared for their Champions League clash with Borussia Dortmund.

And speaking ahead of that match, Arteta confirmed that the Spaniard will not be fit for the visit of Dortmund but his injury is not as bad as first thought.

"He is not fit for tomorrow unfortunately but it doesn't look too serious,” Arteta said.

“We need some more tests tomorrow but it is quite encouraging with the pain that he was showing immediately after the action - we were all quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected."

He added that Raya will not require surgery that “would have kept him out for months”.

“We expected something much worse, as he could almost not handle the amount of pain that he had,” he said. “No need for surgery which was the main fear, so let's see.”

Raya was instrumental in Arsenal ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title last season has carried his stellar form into the current campaign, boasting seven clean sheets in 10 matches prior to Arsenal’s trip to Newcastle.

His injury came on the day Arsenal welcomed William Saliba back to their Premier League matchday squad, with the Frenchman yet to play a minute this season due to a back injury sustained at the World Cup. He was an unused substitute.

The Gunners remain without talismanic winger Bukayo Saka due to a thigh problem suffered against Bayern Munich in October, with Arteta confirming before the Newcastle game that Saka is expected to be out for another four weeks.

Martin Zubimendi is also sidelined with a hamstring problem and is not expected to return until late December.

#928. COP31 went up in flames over fossil fuels — it sends an important message

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Anyone hoping for bold action on climate change has many reasons to be disappointed by the latest United Nations climate summit, COP31, which concluded in a dramatic overtime session on 22 November. After gathering for nearly two weeks in the beach resort city of Antalya, Turkey, in what will probably be the hottest year on record, representatives from nearly all the world’s countries failed to agree on a plan to tackle climate change. Almost 100 nations walked out without signing a ‘cover decision’ — a non-binding statement meant to push for ambitious action — because the document did not call on the world to transition away from fossil fuels.

The last COP climate talk to break down this badly was the Copenhagen summit in 2009. After that meeting, the late geoscientist James Lovelock commented: “I don’t think we’re yet evolved to the point where we’re clever enough to handle as complex a situation as climate change.” Seventeen years and an increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide levels of almost 40 parts per million later, and governments still seem unable to overcome national differences for the benefit of the planet.

The COP31 outcome wasn’t inevitable. There had been some optimism among climate watchers ahead of the summit that, despite ongoing geopolitical conflicts, rising energy prices and energy shortages would spur countries to support a transition away from burning coal, oil and gas — the biggest drivers of climate change. But when language targeting fossil fuels disappeared from the draft cover decision after lobbying by oil-rich nations, a coalition of around 90 countries, led by the European Union and small island states, rejected the agreement.

#927. Champions League power rankings: PSG remain a joke – but who is catching them?

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid are the only teams to still have 100 per cent records after Liverpool’s defeat at Fenerbahce

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

It was largely business as usual last month in the Champions League as Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona kept on scoring and Arsenal and Bayern Munich returned to winning ways while remaining unbeaten.

But the story of the round belonged to Como, who made history by beating Lens 9-1 away from home and equalling the record for the most goals scored in a single Champions League game. Cesc Fabregas’s impressive side now sit fourth in the league phase standings, behind PSG, Real Madrid and Arsenal.

Meanwhile, there was a frustrating defeat for Liverpool at Fenerbahce, but Manchester United produced a stunning comeback to beat Roma and potentially save Michael Carrick’s job, with Matheus Cunha scoring twice on a remarkable night at Old Trafford.

We compiled our 36-team power rankings by combining team’s previous performance in the Champions League, their results in the competition so far, and the likelihood of them going all the way this season.

Agree or disagree with our standings ahead of matchweek five? Let us know and have your say in the comments below.

The reigning champions are making a mockery of suggestions that they are slow starters in the Champions League. Luis Enrique’s back-to-back champions finished outside the top eight in both of their previous successes but have started this campaign on fire in Europe. PSG were 4-0 up after just 17 minutes at Villarreal, and that was without Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. The French champions will be without the brilliant Georgian for the rest of the season after he suffered a ruptured ACL and has been joined on the sidelines by Desire Doue, who suffered the same injury during a 3-2 win over Nice on Saturday.

Defeats to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League and Real Madrid in LaLiga ended their winning start under Hansi Flick and perhaps raised the same concerns over whether their defence holds up come the knockout stages. But Lamine Yamal is arguably the world’s best player on current form and Raphinha isn’t too bad, either. The Brazilian made it an astonishing 19 goals and three assists in just 13 matches across LaLiga and the Champions League with his double in the 3-0 win over Aston Villa at Camp Nou.

Mikel Arteta’s got the result they needed in Prague, even if a difficult second-half performance made it a bit of a struggle. An entertaining draw last time out at Bayern Munich, who have such a strong home record, gave a good account of whether the Premier League champions can take the next step against a heavyweight side in the business end of the Champions League.

Bayern returned to winning ways with a professional win against Atletico Madrid – and the big surprise was that Harry Kane was not on the scoresheet. The Ballon d’Or holder’s 10-match scoring run in the Champions League came to an end at the Metropolitano, missing the chance to equal Cristiano Ronaldo’s record, and Kane will now be out until the “business end” of the season due to an ankle injury.

Perhaps chaos is the new normal under Jose Mourinho. Real Madrid trailed late on in Athens but Kylian Mbappe equalised before Fede Valverde scored a stunning winner in stoppage time. Jude Bellingham also scored an outrageous flick. Somehow with maximum points, despite trailing Roma 3-1 at the Stadio Olimpico, and Inter and RB Leipzig spurning chances to take the lead at the Bernabeu, the 15-time Champions League winners continue to find a way.

Three defeats from four in the Premier League have the shine off an impressive start for Enzo Maresca’s side, while uncertainty off the pitch remains as well. But a battling win at RB Leipzig, with a customary Erling Haaland goal, was a good response, even if City have now gone nine games without a clean sheet in all competitions. Next up: the return of Kevin De Bruyne with Napoli, followed by a mouthwatering trip to Barcelona.

Liverpool have conceded three goals in three consecutive games in the Champions League or European Cup for the first time and the manner of their “messy” collapse against Fenerbahce was a concern. The nature of Liverpool’s squad means Andoni Iraola has needed to rotate in Champions League but Liverpool’s performance in Istanbul underlined the task he faces. In-form Club Brugge can’t be taken lightly after the international break.

Despite defeat in the Camp Nou, you get the feeling that Unai Emery’s new-look Aston Villa will have learned a lot from their meeting with Barcelona. They had moments of threat, too. Bright showings from the refreshed attacking line-up of Nicolas Jackson, Johan Manzambi, Ibrahim Mbaye and Alysson have helped the Europa League winners retaining their identity under Emery despite the huge squad turnover in the summer.

After starting with back-to-back defeats, how badly Inter needed to respond with back-to-back wins. A comfortable win at Feyenoord also came after the Milan derby defeat, with Pio Esposito stepping up amid Lautaro Martinez’s continued absence.

WOW. If Como announced themselves by thrashing Manchester United, the Champions League debutants stole the show this week with a NINE-goal dismantling of poor Lens. Cesc Fabregas’s stylish side became the first team to score nine goals away from home in the Champions League or European Cup since 1971. The Italian side are certainly making a name for themselves. Those games against PSG and Barcelona at the end of the league phase are going to be fascinating.

#926. Alonso heckled as Chelsea are humiliated by Leeds

There are two non-negotiables for Chelsea managers. Do not lose at home to Tottenham Hotspur and do not lose at home to Leeds United. But Xabi Alonso has now completed the nightmare double.

Just as Spurs broke their Stamford Bridge hoodoo a few weeks ago, Leeds secured their first win at Chelsea since 1999 by humiliating the hosts after falling a goal behind.

It was 67 long years since Chelsea had last lost at home to Tottenham and Leeds in the same season, and Alonso was left in no doubt about how seriously supporters take that as his team were loudly booed and he was heckled.

Cole Palmer stormed down the tunnel at full time, ignoring the advice of Chelsea’s so-called “cultural architect” Willie Isa to applaud the remaining home fans, and shrugging off the attention of injured striker João Pedro.

Having been left out of the last England squad, Palmer was largely anonymous for Chelsea but he was not alone and Alonso is already facing similar questions to his predecessors about the team’s mentality.

“I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment, mentally,” Alonso said. “When we receive a punch, we didn’t recover that strong, that tough enough and today that was my feeling.

“The fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high and we feel sorry for them. For sure, it’s not the easiest moment. It’s a fragile moment, but we need to work together and stick together because there is still a long way to go.”

Alonso is yet to name the same starting XI for successive league games and there appears to be no discernible plan or style of play.

Injuries have contributed to Chelsea’s unremarkable start to the season under Alonso – and Moisés Caicedo was forced off early in the first half – but the problems run deeper than the treatment table.

Alonso’s defence has now conceded 20 goals, which has contributed to Chelsea losing five league games already – more than Manchester United. In between three defeats in their last four league games, Chelsea were also knocked out of the Carabao Cup.

The Spaniard had answered questions about Chelsea’s identity, or lack of it, by saying he wanted his team to be competitive. But they were anything but against a Leeds side who had seven more shots than their hosts and five more on target.

It is hard to fathom how, through all the chopping and changing, Wesley Fofana still starts games for Chelsea in defence. It was his pathetic attempted header, which bounced backwards towards his own goal, that contributed to Noah Okafor’s first goal.

Josh Acheampong also got himself into a mess and Okafor was somehow able to squeeze a shot past goalkeeper Emi Martínez despite having three Chelsea players around him.

Chelsea had taken the lead through striker Emmanuel Emegha, on his first start for the club, but from that moment on they were second best with Leeds pair Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka running the middle of the park.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin had hit the crossbar and failed to find the net with three more presentable opportunities in the first half, but he took his chance from the penalty spot eight minutes after the break.

Morgan Rogers had argued that James Justin’s shot hit him too far up his arm for it to be a penalty, but a VAR check upheld referee Michael Oliver’s decision and Calvert-Lewin kept his cool.

That should have been the moment that shook Chelsea into action and prompted a response but, instead, Alonso’s team fell apart and he was unable to provoke a shift in momentum from the touchline.

Just five minutes after Calvert-Lewin had put Leeds ahead, Okafor effectively sealed the victory by firing the ball into the net after Chelsea had failed to deal with a long throw into their penalty area.

Noah Okafor's brace helps seal Leeds' first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge since 1999! 💥 https://t.co/UAmsJziJmZ

“I can’t wait to be on the sofa with coffee and cake and also watch this game back because it was a really good game,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds head coach, said. “I was a bit disappointed even at half-time when it was just a draw, because I think we were the better side from the first to the last.”

John Terry still works with Chelsea’s academy and it might be worth Alonso getting the former captain to speak to the club’s senior players about how to defend and compete. Whatever has been done on the training pitch so far has not worked.

Alonso’s substitutes are yet to register a single goal or assist in the league this season and his changes failed to make any sort of impact here. For the visitors, however, two substitutes combined to score their fourth goal in time added on for stoppages.

Harry Wilson played in Brenden Aaronson and, from a tight angle, he managed to find the back of the net by sending the ball through the legs of Martínez.

The home stands were already half-empty by that point, but some supporters hung around to show their displeasure and Palmer could not contain his anger.

We know what the history of this game is like and what the fans expect - we know they have wanted a win here for a long time. It’s right we can enjoy this performance.

Frank’s start to life at Palace begins with defeat but an improved display. Coventry are up to 13th with their fourth win of the season.

Another home win for Tottenham, who managed the game well and introduced a new star to the Premier League in Williams-Barnett

What a day for Leeds. They scored four and it could have been more. For Chelsea, they lost their way when Caicedo went off and without Joao Pedro, they have lost their spark in attack.

Bournemouth make it nine wins in a row in all competitions after doing enough in the first half to get the job done.

Leeds finish the match in style as Aaronson puts the seal on an impressive away day.

It’s all over and Sunderland deservedly leave with a point. Villa will be very disappointed by their display.

What was I saying in the last post?! The home side are on the attack Thomas-Asante pokes a shot at goal and forces Henderson into a save but hits his own player McNeil, who bundles the ball in the net.

Can Chelsea stage a late fightback? Will we get a winner between Coventry and Palace?

Needing a goal, Emery makes a bold decision to take off Villa’s top scorer and bring on Madjo.

Despite the two-goal lead and the magnificent debut performance of Luca Williams-Barnett, the home support has remained subdued throughout the afternoon.

At times, the shouts of two children sat just behind the press box feel like by far the loudest noise in the stadium - although that might just be proximity.

Much quieter half at the CBS Arena but Palace are more likely to get a third goal.

This has gone from bad to worse for Chelsea. One supporter near the dug-outs was so angry at Leeds scoring a third goal that he got up and screamed his displeasure at manager Xabi Alonso.

1999 was the last time Leeds won at Chelsea. Today looks like they will get another, as Okafor takes advantage of more poor defending to finish past Martinez.

Villa’s fans are now chanting loudly for substitute John McGinn to be introduced.

They are getting their wish, too, as the Scotland international is coming on with winger Ibrahim Mbaye.

Morgan Rogers and Chelsea are pretty upset about that penalty being awarded to Leeds. They felt the ball struck him too far up his arm to be a penalty. Calvert-Lewin took his spot-kick superbly and it’s gone very, very quiet among the home fans.

Everything Luca Williams-Barnett touches is turning to gold today. He has a goal to his name already, and adds an assist just six minutes into the second half.

From almost the halfway line, he drove forward, weaving his way expertly into the box before picking out Dominic Solanke in the middle of the box, who tapped the ball into the back of the net.

However, the atmosphere is still a touch subdued, despite James Maddison urging the crowd to make themselves heard almost immediately after the goal, the noise drops to almost a murmur.

Rogers blocks Bogle’s drive with his arm and Michael Oliver gives a penalty to Leeds. After a long check, VAR confirms it.

Calvert-Lewin steps up and sends Martinez the wrong way. The away team deserves this. They have been the better side. That is Calvert-Lewin’s 100th club career goal.

Williams-Barnet gets one-on-one with Furlong and gets past him with ease before firing a cross for Solanke to finish.

The whistle blows for the second half around the grounds. What will the second 45 minutes have for us?

A real lack of quality here from both teams, and Sunderland deserve credit for weathering the early pressure.

Villa appear short of creativity and have managed only one shot on target in the first-half.

Sunderland have defended resolutely and caused Villa’s back-four some problems in the rare moments they have attacked.

Unai Emery marched into the dressing room after the half-time whistle and has much to ponder.

Some boos from the Chelsea fans at half-time. Calvert-Lewin could have had a hat-trick in that first half, sending one header against the bar, two too close to Martinez and flicking a shot just wide. Leeds also had a goal ruled out for offside.

Chelsea just stopped playing after taking the lead.

That half was all about Luca Williams-Barnett. The 18-year-old scored in his first start, and had two opportunities to add to his tally just before the break. He had a header tipped over the bar by Christian Walton and a chance from close range stopped on the line. The future looks bright, as they say.

However, Tottenham faded after a strong opening 15 minutes, and Ipswich were able to break up play and get forward more, exploiting the home side’s lack of a defensive midfielder, and that will be something for Roberto De Zerbi to address in the break.

We have whistles around the ground. That was breathless stuff.

The visitors will feel they should be in front at the break. First, Muharemovic thinks he has scored when he head in a cross from Justin but he was offside.

Then Ampadu’s long throw finds Calvert-Lewin in space and his shot is saved by Martinez. Should have done better there.

Bournemouth finish the half in style. Kluivert gets the second when he taps in a cross from Tavernier.

Palace hit back again. Pino clips a cross to Larsen at the far post and he heads past Rushworth coolly.

Courtesy of Opta: Aged 18 years and 51 days, Luca Williams-Barnett is Tottenham Hotspur’s youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007 (18y 47d).

Villa are in desperate need of a spark and one has to wonder when John McGinn will be introduced. McGinn is on the bench today and the home team are crying out for some inspiration.

Villa did start brilliantly, yet the game has now petered out into a mess of misplaced passes and poor decision-making.

Still no clean sheet for Emi Martinez. But Noah Okafor’s goal wasn’t his fault – he was let down by some bad defending from Wesley Fofana and Josh Acheampong.

Martinez did start Chelsea’s 2-0 victory over Everton, but he didn’t last the full game as he had to be replaced because of injury.

A touch of Hollywood royalty in attendance at Tottenham on this cold November afternoon with Sir Kenneth Branagh and Ryan Reynolds in attendance.

Reynolds is a co-owner of Wrexham, who are currently playing in the Championship at Lincoln City, but he has chosen to watch football in north London instead.

Sakamoto puts Palace back in front with a brilliant finish. Rudoni gets away from Khalaili and crosses to the Japan international. Sakamoto brings it down nicely then rifles a shot into the top corner.

That lead did not last long for Chelsea. The away side hit back within three minutes as Okafor shoots through the legs of Colwill and into the net.

Another full debutant and another goal. This time at Stamford Bridge as Emegha latches onto a ball from Rogers and blasts an unstoppable shot from distance.

Emegha had to wait a while to make his first start for Chelsea, but he’s marked it with a really well taken goal. Leeds will be disappointed with the time and space he and Morgan Rogers, who provided the assist, were given, but it was a good finish.

Caicedo just can’t get going this season. That back injury that forced him off the pitch for a minute earlier has now resulted in him having to be replaced by Jordan Henderson. That’s a real blow to Alonso and Chelsea.

Villa were completely dominant in the opening ten minutes but Sunderland have now managed to subdue the home team.

Johan Manzambi and Nicolas Jackson are both impressing for the home team. Villa do appear a little vulnerable in defence when Sunderland do break forward.

Today will be a day that 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett will not forget in a hurry, he has been energetic since the start and marked his maiden Premier League start with an early goal.

The actual goal might have been a tap-in, but it has injected life into the crowd who had otherwise been largely subdued from the start.

Confusion on the touchline for Chelsea. Caicedo was down after hurting his back. Alonso tried to stop his phyisos going straight on to the pitch, but referee Michael Oliver called them on. That meant Caicedo had to spend a minute off the pitch under the latest rules.

Remember this moment because on his first senior start Williams-Barnet has made it a special one with goal. It was scrappy but he will not care. The Tottenham fans have been talking about his young fan for a long time.

Equaliser for Palace and Frank. Very good response from his players as Larsen flicks the ball to Pino and the Spain international fires into the net.

No shots on target from either side but it is already shaping up to be attack vs defence. Villa are dominating the goal and looking threatening.

Awoniyi is through one-on-one with Henderson, goes around the keeper but Disasi does brilliantly to recover and make the block.

Worst possible start for Frank and Palace as Awoniyi gets his second goal of the season with a cool finish.

A video of De Zerbi saying “let’s go” in a manner that might be more at home in American Football is shown before the teams come out onto the pitch.

The atmosphere feels a bit subdued so far, but it is an important match for Tottenham.

This is probably the kiss of death from me, but I’m really looking forward to watching Tarik Muharemovic today. The defender has impressed me every time I’ve watched Leeds on television this season and looks to be one of the signings of the summer. Dare I say it, but Chelsea could have done worse than sign him given their troubles at the back. Emi Martinez is back in goal for the home side. He’s yet to keep a clean sheet since signing from Aston Villa.

Thomas Frank declared “it’s good to be back in the circus” of football management ahead of his first match as Crystal Palace boss.

The 53-year-old Dane admitted he could have easily spent a few more months sipping wine, “eating too well” and collecting passport stamps, but something resonated when he asked his wife why he was tempted to seek out a new job and she told him, “(It’s) because you can’t help yourself”.

Frank hinted that there was more behind the story to his disappointing spell at Tottenham he might one day reveal, but for now he has a team to rescue from a relegation fight, beginning with today’s trip to Coventry.

If you don’t learn from any of your jobs, I don’t think you reflect, I don’t think you improve, and I don’t think you get better.

Of course there’s a lot of things I have been reflecting over. The details, that will be for another time, but I can say I’ve learned, definitely.

I was very aware I didn’t want to do anything in the summer. I put a statement out there, I needed more time. I can actually, honestly say I would have been fine if it was three, four, five, six, seven months more, because it’s good to be back in the circus, but it’s also unbelievably good not to be in, especially if you enjoy life, which I do.

I was spending time with family and friends and doing all that, but I think the club, the way Palace is, how well Steve Parish especially spoke about the club and ideas, Matt Hobbs and Iain Moody and these guys, too, helped convince me it was a good idea.

Construction news: work on the North Stand behind one of the Villa Park goals continues to progress.

There are clear structural changes since Villa’s last home game and a mural of fans makes it more appealing to look at.

This stand is scheduled to be ready for next season and will increase Villa’s capacity to over 50,000.

Tottenham’s impressive run of form came to a crashing halt with a 1-0 defeat to Leeds just before the international break, but manager Roberto De Zerbi will be hoping for a fresh start - even if he will not be pitchside after picking up a second yellow card of the season.

De Zerbi made six changes from the aforementioned defeat to Leeds, including a first start for teenager Luca Williams-Barnett, a player who has come through the club’s academy.

There is no place in the squad for Sandro Tonali or Tosin Adarabioyo, but James Maddison will start for the first time since the 2-0 defeat to Chelsea in October.

Aston Villa 2.0 was always likely to be a slow-burner, and it is proving exactly that for Unai Emery.

His team has impressed and underwhelmed in equal measure so far this season but this is an opportunity to hoist themselves up the table.

A clean sheet would be a good starting point, as they have not secured a shutout in front of their own fans in the league since March.

There is no Alejandro Garnacho or Tammy Abraham in the matchday squad today.

Good afternoon and welcome to coverage from the Premier League as domestic football returns after an international break.

We have five matches to bring you, including Chelsea vs Leeds, Aston Villa vs Sunderland and Tottenham vs Ipswich.

Xabi Alonso said his Chelsea side needs to learn to deal with the absence of Joao Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals in the absence of their injured striker.

The Brazilian has not played since the 2-0 win over Everton on October 17 and will be unavailable again today.

Without a focal point in the number nine position, Chelsea’s goal output has been dramatically reduced and they have dropped to fifth and having suffered two defeats in their last three games.

“(We need) the whole team for that,” said Alonso. “It’s not just the strikers that can score. We can score from set-pieces, from defenders, from midfielders.

“It’s teamwork. For sure Joao is an important player but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.

“We need to deal with it. It’s not that I’m going to look for one explanation. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.”

Tottenham will not have their manager, Roberto De Zerbi, on the touchline after receiving three yellow cards this season.

Gary O’Neil is targeting a “special” result at Tottenham, but promised Ipswich will not make any drastic changes after a four-match winless run.

Ipswich lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth before the two-week break, which followed draws with Hull and Nottingham Forest along with a narrow defeat at Manchester City, but O’Neil is happy with his new-look group.

“There won’t be any drastic changes. The odd personnel change, (but) I don’t think it’s going to be a big shift for us,” O’Neil told a press conference.

“It’s a very well-balanced squad. There’s going to be no massive uplifts or downgrades when we have to change players within this group.”

Aston Villa will have Johan Manzambi available for the visit of Sunderland.

The midfielder did not feature for Switzerland during the recent international break because of a calf injury but he has trained with the rest of the squad and can feature today.

Villa can also call on right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka after a muscle injury ruled him out for six matches. His return is timely as Matty Cash is unavailable.

Cash was suspended for Villa’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United before the international break but suffered a concussion while away with Poland.

#925. Turkey uses espionage accusations to pressure government critics

The arrest of a German foundation's employee in Istanbul this week has put the focus back on pressure tactics used by the Erdogan administration. The arrest is far from the first of its kind.

When police officers appeared at her home in Istanbul last Wednesday evening, Yonca Verdioglu Sik was surprised — even more so when they took her in for questioning. Her lawyer says she was accused of political and military espionage.

But, according to transcripts of the interrogation that were published later, Verdioglu Sik was never asked any questions about espionage. Instead the public prosecutor's office appeared to be more interested in the activities of her German employer, the Heinrich Böll Foundation.

For 18 years, Verdioglu Sik, who was born and raised in Germany, has been the foundation's project coordinator. In her role, she organizes projects that focus on democracy and the rights of women, minorities and LGBTQ+ people.

During the interrogation, transfers of money from the foundation into her bank account were discussed. Verdioglu Sik found out that she was now also subject to a travel ban.

Verdioglu Sik was eventually released, but her arrest caused outrage among critics of the Turkish government. She is married to investigative journalist and member of parliament, Ahmet Sik. He belongs to the left-wing Workers' Party of Turkey, or TIP, and is known as one of the harshest critics of the current government.

Sik has recently been looking into a stock market scandal, which allegedly benefited members of the ruling Justice and Development Party, or AKP, headed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and associates.

Opposition critics drew a clear conclusion: As a member of parliament, Sik has parliamentary immunity. So instead, the justice system is putting pressure on him through his wife.

"If you take away a state's law, what is left is no longer called a state, but a gang," Sik responded to the arrest in writing.

Verdioglu Sik's arrest is not the first such case in Turkey. Ever since the attempted coup against the Erdogan government in 2016, accusations of espionage have been leveled at a wide variety of groups in Turkey: journalists, opposition figures and human rights activists as well as employees of foreign embassies and staff of foreign institutions like nongovernmental organizations and foundations.

Such accusations have often been followed by acquittals or convictions for other offenses, albeit sometimes years later. But what the many instances have in common is what's known as a "chilling effect." Any investigation can mean lengthy pre-trial detention, reputational and professional damage and even social isolation.

In the past, such cases have even triggered diplomatic spats.

In 2015, for example, Can Dundar and Erdem Gul, both senior journalists at the opposition daily Cumhuriyet, were accused of espionage after reporting that Turkey had tried to ship arms to rebels fighting the Syrian government. Dundar now lives in exile in Berlin.

In 2017, Erdogan said that reporter Deniz Yücel, then working for German newspaper Die Welt, was a "German agent." That led to a serious diplomatic crisis between Berlin and Ankara.

Espionage charges have also been laid against local employees of the US diplomatic corps and against a lawyer working for the German embassy. US pastor Andrew Brunson and his wife were also arrested because of alleged links to Kurdish anti-government groups. Turkish philanthropist and human rights activist Osman Kavala, who was charged with espionage and attempting to overthrow the constitutional order, remains in prison.

Most recently, espionage charges have been brought against the former Istanbul mayor and Erdogan's political competitor, Ekrem Imamoglu, and a number of journalists.

Hakki Tas, a research fellow and expert on Turkey at the German Institute for Global and Area Studies, said the number of such cases have been increasing over the past few years.

On the one hand, Turkey has the right to protect itself from foreign intelligence services — especially given geopolitical competition and conflict in the region, he argued. On the other hand, there's a long tradition of bringing the Turkish opposition to court to face security charges.

"What foreigners or employees of foreign institutions have experienced in recent years is a continuation of this pattern," Tas told DW.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Media outlets and NGOs critical of the government have faced investigations, trials and other sorts of state sanctions for years. The ruling AKP party has also brought in its own version of a so-called "foreign agent law."

These sorts of espionage cases serve both a domestic and foreign policy function, Tas said.

For locals, "contact with a foreign institution, foreign funding or even a perfectly normal salary could become part of an investigation someday," he explained. "For opposition figures and civil society organizations, in particular, this can become a security issue."

In terms of foreign policy, the cases also show other countries that there are limits to their activities inside Turkey. These kinds of accusations seem to become more frequent when there's some sort of foreign policy tension — for example, after Western criticism of how opposition groups were dealt with after the alleged coup in 2016, the aforementioned disputes about arms deliveries in connection with Syria, or criticism from abroad about the removal of elected mayors in Turkey.

It can also serve as a kind of "hostage diplomacy," Tas said.

The case of US pastor Brunson is a good example. After his arrest, the Turkish government proposed a trade with the Americans. They wanted to exchange Turkish preacher Fethullah Gulen, who lived in the US and who the Turkish government blamed for the 2016 coup attempt.

This suspicion of foreign institutions isn't something that the Erdogan government invented, Tas points out. In the early 2000s, several representatives of German organizations were already made to stand trial in Turkey. At the time, it was alleged that, among other things, the German spy service was using German foundations as a front for conspiracy.

In some of the best-known cases, defendants often don't end up convicted of espionage. In the case of activist Osman Kavala, he was initially acquitted of espionage several times and spent two years in prison, just because of those charges.

But Tas said that's no surprise, referring to a 1979 work about the sociology of law written by US law professor Malcolm Feeley. It's title: "The Process Is the Punishment."

This article was originally written in German.

Brentford 4-0 Everton: The Bees moved into the top six after dismantling David Moyes’ side on Monday night

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Vitaly Janelt scored a spectacular 30-yard goal as Brentford cruised to an emphatic 4-0 victory against 10-man Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium.

A run of just one victory in five outings had caused early-season optimism surrounding Keith Andrews’ team to fade, but this was a resolute performance to propel them to sixth in the Premier League. Culpability for Everton’s collapse rested largely with James Tarkowski, sent off in the 40th minute following a dangerous challenge on Yehor Yarmolyuk.

David Moyes was setting a record for matches in charge of Everton, his 593rd game surpassing the historic tally set by Harry Catterick during the 1960s and 1970s. Yet a miserable opening half ensured it was an ordeal rather than a celebration.

Virtually everything went wrong for the visitors. Both of Brentford’s initial goals, scored by Keane Lewis-Potter, came via deflections, and Tarkowski’s temporary abandonment of responsibility - lunging studs-first into Yarmolyuk’s shin with his side two goals down - proved impossible for Moyes to mitigate. He was badly let down by a senior figure in a time of need.

Thereafter, the fixture offered little competition. The match might have drifted toward a standard two-goal victory for Brentford had Janelt not delivered a brilliant strike from distance that whistled past Jordan Pickford to compound the misery for Moyes and Tarkowski alike.

Fabio Carvalho turned the ball over the goal-line using his knee during stoppage time, providing the final indignity for Everton.

Brentford were impressive throughout. In the early stages, Callum Wilson picked out Michael Kayode making a run up the right side; the full-back was presented with a clear sight of Pickford’s goal but dragged his strike wide across the face.

Everton were making it far too easy. Midway through the half, they failed to cope with a ball over the top, allowing Jaidon Anthony to send a low pass into the middle with a deft touch. It was a controlled first-time delivery that found Lewis-Potter in space, his shot spinning in off Jarrad Branthwaite.

It required less than two minutes for Lewis-Potter to add a near-identical second, as a delivery into the box from Mikkel Damsgaard exposed fragile Everton defending.

The Brentford player was afforded two opportunities, his initial attempt rebounding back to him before squeezing the ball home at the second attempt via a deflection off Thierno Barry.

Everton were sinking and their captain abandoned them to their fate. Tarkowski was initially handed only a yellow card for a studs-up challenge on Yarmolyuk. However, a single look at the replay confirmed the tackle was far more serious, making high contact on Yarmolyuk’s standing leg, rendering his sending-off inevitable.

Jack Grealish was introduced to try to lift Everton, making his first appearance following a five-game absence due to disciplinary matters.

It made no difference. When Janelt’s 30-yard rocket flew past Pickford midway through the second half, it signalled the moment for several away supporters to start the long journey home, leaving few behind to witness Carvalho’s late tap-in on a chastening night for their club.

League Two player Isiah Noel-Williams has been charged with three counts of rape.

Noel-Williams, who plays for Barnet, was remanded in custody as part of a police investigation by Hertfordshire Constabulary’s Public Protection Command, which has now confirmed charges against the footballer.

The 23-year-old from St Albans has also been charged with assault by penetration, engaging in sexual communication with a child, and supplying a controlled drug (Class B).

Noel-Williams appeared at Hatfield Magistrates’ Court on Saturday 21 November where he was taken into custody.

He will next appear at St Albans Crown Court on Tuesday 22 December.

Barnet put out a statement before the charges were made public, writing on their website: “The club is co-operating fully with the authorities and will determine any further action in due course.

“As this is now a matter for the courts, the club will not be making any further comment.”

This season was Noel-Williams’ first in the Football League, joining Barnet from non-league side Hemel Hempstead in the summer.

The striker has made nine appearances across all competitions and is yet to register a goal contribution.

He has previously played for a number of non-league clubs including Kettering Town, Matlock Town and Harrow Borough.

Noel-Williams was sent off in a 1-1 draw with Oldham in October, with manager Dean Brennan branding the red card a “farce”, and he subsequently received racist abuse which Barnet condemned “in the strongest terms”.

Barnet are vying for promotion this term and sit second in League Two, trailing leaders Salford City by four points.
